Only known backer is South Park Commons (accelerator-style check). No publicly announced round found. Note: the A$11M seed for Melbourne's 'exteRNA' (RNA cancer therapies) is a different company.

companies.name: Manna AI
companies.funding_notes: Manna AI (SPC page links dreem-world.ai; company site manna-world.com), San Francisco; building Dreem, an AI-native interactive storytelling/entertainment platform with persistent AI characters and branching story worlds (iOS app 'Dreem - Interactive Stories'); founded 2026. Only known backer is South Park Commons; a tracker shows an undisclosed early-stage deal around Jan 2026 consistent with the SPC check. No publicly announced round, amount or other investors found.

companies.name: Butterbase
companies.funding_notes: Butterbase (butterbase.ai, linked from its SPC page), San Francisco; agent-native backend/infrastructure platform for AI-native services firms (CRM, intake, portals, invoicing, auth, storage, AI gateway, MCP); founded 2025. Only known backer is South Park Commons; a tracker lists an undisclosed early-stage VC deal. No publicly announced round, amount or other investors found.

companies.name: Chip
companies.description: Chip is the first mass-market American robot, he just happens to be your car.
companies.funding_notes: Chip Motors (chipmotors.com, linked from its SPC page), Miami-based (hiring in Los Angeles and Miami); 'Chip', a street-legal 25-mph low-speed electric 'life utility vehicle' with teleoperated self-parking ('Chip Go!'), $15k-18k, reservations open, deliveries planned 2027 (The Verge, Jul 17, 2026); CEO Jameson Detweiler. Outside VC money beyond SPC: Old Tom Capital ('The Club by Old Tom Capital') lists Chip Motors in its portfolio, and social posts (not used as sources) indicate Morrison Seger Venture Capital Partners also invested around early-mid 2026. No press release or reputable news discloses round type, amount or date.

companies.name: Nyquis
companies.description: Catching faults before they catch fire
companies.funding_notes: Nyquis (nyquis.com, linked from its SPC page), San Francisco; AI point-on-wave grid-monitoring sensors (Nyquis Nodes) at substations to detect high-impedance faults before outages/wildfires, piloting in New Mexico; founder David Gobaud (also Senior Venture Partner at Pioneer Fund; ex-Yoshi, Mobius Network). Startuply.vc (Jul 2026) calls it 'Pioneer Fund-backed'; social posts (not used as sources) around May 2026 name Pioneer Fund, Taro Fukuyama, South Park Commons and Gigascale Capital as investors, and trackers describe it as a seed round, but no press release or reputable news confirms round type, amount or date. Founder's ties to Pioneer Fund noted.

companies.name: Pillar Space Systems
companies.funding_notes: Pillar Space Systems (pillarspace.com, linked from its SPC page), New York; reusable LEO satellites rented as 'standing infrastructure' to host customer payloads (power, data, thermal, mobility, docking; return capsules for microgravity manufacturing); founded 2026. Only known backer is South Park Commons. No publicly announced round found. Note: the $3.8M pre-seed (Sep 2025) and a16z-led $20M seed (Apr 2026) for 'Pillar' belong to unrelated companies (incl. a financial-risk-management platform).

companies.name: Qosmic
companies.description: The optical highway to the cosmos
companies.funding_notes: QOSMIC (qosmic.space, linked from its SPC page), Bengaluru; laser/optical ground stations and satellite optical terminals ('highway to the cosmos'), incubated at ARTPARK (IISc); founded 2025 by Shreyaans Jain (CEO), Rohit Ramakrishnan and Aloke Kumar; co-designing terminals with TakeMe2Space. Raised a $3.33M seed co-led by Accel and Prosus (Ventures), with South Park Commons, ARTPARK and angel Manish Jain (company release published on SpaceNews, dated Jul 15, 2026; SPC's June 30, 2026 update already reported the raise, so announcement was ~late Jun-mid Jul 2026). Also in Accel Atoms portfolio. Total equity = $3.33M (sum of sourced rounds).

companies.name: Lys
companies.description: Building the humanistic path to the merge.
companies.funding_notes: Lys Technologies (lys.inc, linked from its SPC page), reportedly based in Sofia, Bulgaria (SPC lists 'Other'); non-invasive brain-computer interface using optical neuroimaging (fNIRS/DOT) wearable for human-AI interaction ('the humanistic path to the merge'); founded 2025. Only known backer is South Park Commons; a tracker shows an undisclosed early-stage VC deal ~Sep 2026 with SPC as investor. No publicly announced round, amount or other investors found.

companies.name: Equivariant Systems
companies.funding_notes: Equivariant Systems (equivariantsystems.com, linked from its SPC page), San Francisco; multi-physics modeling/simulation software for semiconductors (first product 'Fermi'); founder/CEO Daanish Shabbir; founded 2025, SPC 2025 cohort. Only known backer is South Park Commons. A tracker labels its latest deal 'seed' with no amount or investors; StartupDB/Tracxn show no rounds. No press release or reputable news of a priced round found.

companies.name: Scriben
companies.funding_notes: Scriben (scriben.ai, linked from its SPC page), San Francisco; AI ballpoint pen that records in-person conversations offline and turns them into work memory and approval-gated actions (CRM, email, calendar), with companion iOS app; founded 2026. Its press page cites only 'Backed by South Park Commons' plus 2026 design awards (MUSE, American Good Design, London Design Awards) and Digital Trends coverage. No publicly announced round, amount or other investors found.

companies.name: First Contact
companies.description: Giving robots a sense of touch
companies.funding_notes: First Contact (firstcontact.xyz; SPC page links no website, matched by name, SF location and tactile-robotics description; reportedly formerly 'Ontologian'), San Francisco; tactile-sensing gloves for robot data capture (847 taxels/hand at 240 Hz, Python SDK, $3,000/pair early batch, pre-orders open); team includes Kavan McEachern and Krithika Shamanna. Only known backer is South Park Commons; an advisor's social post (not used) claims to be the 'first investor'. No publicly announced round found. Caveat: a podcast mentioning a YC pre-seed and recent seed refers to 6thSense, a different tactile company, not First Contact.

companies.name: Human Computer Lab
companies.funding_notes: Human Computer Lab (humancomputerlab.com, linked from its SPC page), San Francisco with team in Canada/US; expressive home robots, first product the LeLamp robot lamp. Solo founder Shahvir Sarkary; started June 2025. BetaKit (Nov 2025) reports a $500K USD pre-seed SAFE led by South Park Commons and FR8 (Finnish tech residency), later extended by another $900K SAFE from the same investors, bringing the round to $1.4M USD; the company's own update says the pre-seed closed Aug 2025. All SAFE/pre-seed money (includes SPC's Founder Fellowship-style check); no priced seed or later round public. Exact date of the $900K extension not published.

companies.name: Fieldworks AI
companies.funding_notes: Fieldworks AI (fieldworks.ai, linked from its SPC page), Austin, Texas (SPC lists San Francisco); AI-native construction management for large capital projects, says it supports more than $1B in active projects. Founders Audrey Bascoul and Michael Surowiec; founded 2025. Only known backer is South Park Commons (founder announced the SPC backing Oct 2025), whose early check is an accelerator-style investment, not a priced round. No press release or reputable news of a round or amount found; trackers' 'seed' labels are not supported by a public source.

companies.name: June
companies.funding_notes: June (tryjune.ai, linked from its SPC page), San Francisco; AI event-design tool that turns a text prompt into visual design boards and orders from rental vendors. Founders Irfan-ali Manji and Paul Crouther; founded 2024. No public funding beyond SPC's early accelerator-style check. Caveat: not the same company as the enterprise-software 'June AI' that announced a ~$20M pre-seed in Aug 2026 (GlobeNewswire/TechCrunch); that is a different startup and was excluded.

companies.name: Captify
companies.description: Building captions for real life, delivered through smart glasses
companies.funding_notes: Captify (captify.glass, linked from its SPC page), San Francisco Bay Area; prescription-ready AI captioning smart glasses for deaf/hard-of-hearing people. Founders Tom Pritsky and Jason Gui; founded 2025. Finalist and Audience Choice winner of the 2026 VSP Vision Innovation Challenge (Mar 13 2026, Vision Expo); VSP said selected startups could potentially get a $400K THINC Ventures investment, but no award or investment to Captify was announced. No press release or reputable news of a priced round or amount; only SPC's early accelerator-style check is evident (a paid tracker lists undisclosed seed deals, not used). Not to be confused with UK adtech company Captify (captifytechnologies.com).

companies.name: Duplex AI
companies.description: Natural, full-duplex voice AI for enterprises
companies.website_source: company website (domain verified against name and accelerator description)
companies.funding_notes: Duplex AI (duplexai.io, input website), San Francisco; full-duplex, low-latency speech-to-speech voice AI for enterprises. Founders reported as Xutai Ma and Anna Sun; founded 2026; presented at SPC's Summer 2026 Demo Faire. Only known backer is South Park Commons (accelerator-style early check; trackers record an undisclosed July 2026 early-stage deal). No press release or reputable news of a round or amount.

companies.name: AI Theresa
companies.website_source: company website (domain verified against name and accelerator description)
companies.funding_notes: AI Theresa (aitheresa.ai, input website), San Francisco; 'self-evolving AI forward deployed engineer' that observes company workflows and builds/runs AI automations (sold as FDE-as-a-service). Founded 2026; part of SPC's Summer 2026 Demo Faire cohort. Only known backer is South Park Commons (accelerator-style early check; trackers note an undisclosed July 2026 deal). No press release or reputable news of a round or amount.

companies.name: Portal
companies.description: Share your product as a link
companies.funding_notes: Portal (makeportals.com, linked from its SPC page; SPC F25), San Francisco; lets teams share a live, isolated cloud-browser session of their product (localhost, extensions, demo accounts) as a link, with analytics and optional AI guide. Founder Zachary Goldman; founded 2025. No public funding beyond SPC's early accelerator-style check; no press release or news of a round.

companies.name: Ranvier Systems
companies.description: Neuromorphic hardware for training foundation models
companies.funding_notes: Ranvier Systems, New York; neuromorphic hardware for training event-based foundation models. Founders Christian Pehle and William Ludington; founded 2026; presented at SPC's Summer 2026 Demo Faire. No official website verified (SPC page links none; a 'Ranvier-Systems' GitHub org hosts an LLM inference router and could not be confirmed as the same company). No public funding beyond SPC's early accelerator-style check.

companies.name: Vitrus
companies.description: Making robot development as programmable as software
companies.funding_notes: Vitrus (vitrus.com, linked from its SPC page; Vitrus Inc.), San Francisco/Palo Alto; multimodal AI and robotics platform for architecture, construction and autonomous fabrication ('machines that make machines'). Founder Lucas Cassiano; SPC lists 2024. Only trackers report funding (e.g. a $400K Dec 2024 pre-seed tied to SPC, and conflicting totals up to ~$1M including a 2023 round); none confirmed by a press release or reputable news, so no amounts recorded. Any SPC money is an accelerator-style check, not a priced round.

companies.name: Asymptote Labs
companies.funding_notes: Asymptote Labs (asymptotelabs.ai, linked from its SPC page), New York/San Francisco; security and runtime data layer for AI coding agents (agent telemetry, detection and response, policy controls). Co-founders Justin D'Souza (CEO) and Shukan Shah (CTO), both ex-Doppel; founded 2025. Its About page says it is backed by South Park Commons plus ~20 named operator angels (e.g. Feross Aboukhadijeh, Akshat Bubna, Aditya Agarwal, Kevin Tian, Ruchi Sanghvi). Amount, date and round type not published; trackers call a Jan 2026 round 'seed' (and list Tower Research Ventures), but no press release or reputable news confirms a priced round, so treated as SPC + angel money.

companies.name: Dentronic
companies.description: AI-powered robotic assistants for dental clinics
companies.funding_notes: Dentronic Inc. (dentronic.ai, linked from its SPC page), Silicon Valley/San Francisco; chairside AI robotic dental assistant arm 'Dexer/Dexor' (suction, retraction). CEO Choi Kyung-yeon with co-founders Lee Minjun and Choi Soyoon; founded 2026 per SPC. ChosunBiz (Mar 19 2026) reports selection for SPC's Founder Fellowship and a $1M (~KRW 1.5B) pre-seed investment; Krew Capital also lists Dentronic in its portfolio (SPC as co-investor), and Krew's participation in that pre-seed is inferred, not stated. Pre-seed only; no priced seed or later round public.

companies.name: Kit
companies.funding_notes: Kit (Kit.com), San Francisco; physician-ordered at-home diagnostic test kits processed in its own CLIA-certified, CAP-accredited San Francisco lab. Founders Philip Fung (CEO) and Erik Salazar (COO). Acquired by Ro (Roman Health) on June 30, 2021 (Ro press release; price undisclosed). TechCrunch reported Kit had raised only a $3.3M seed round before the acquisition, from Expa, Sherpalo Ventures, South Park Commons, Slow Ventures and Village Global; caveat: TechCrunch attributed that figure to Crunchbase, and no lead or date for the seed was published. Domain from Ro's release (SPC page links none).

companies.name: Producer
companies.funding_notes: Producer / ProducerAI (producer.ai, linked from its SPC page; formerly Riffusion), San Francisco; conversational AI music-creation agent. Founders Seth Forsgren (CEO) and Hayk Martiros. Raised a $4M seed (TechCrunch, Oct 17 2023) led by Greycroft with South Park Commons and Sky9; caveat: Sky9's own Feb 2026 release says Sky9 led the seed alongside SPC and Greycroft. SPC's page also lists Felicis and Spark Capital as other investors, but no public source gives a round or amount for them. Acquired by Google (team joined Google Labs/DeepMind) on Feb 24, 2026; price undisclosed. A tracker mentions a 2024 'Series A2' with no amount; not confirmed by a reputable source, so total is the sourced $4M seed only.

companies.name: DoubleLoop
companies.website_source: company website (domain verified against name and accelerator description)
companies.funding_notes: DoubleLoop (doubleloop.app, input website; Double-Loop, Inc., Albany, CA), Bay Area; software linking product work and metric trees to business outcomes. Founders Dan Schmidt (CEO) and Sumit Gupta. Acquired by Mixpanel on Oct 7, 2025 (BusinessWire / Mixpanel blog; terms undisclosed). Two SEC Form D notices filed Apr 28, 2023 report equity sales of $1,383,287 (first sale Oct 28, 2019) and $1,619,500 (first sale Oct 4, 2022, Rule 506(c)), $3,002,787 combined; the filings don't say whether these were priced rounds or SAFEs, and no press release names a seed. Investors per SPC's page/trackers include South Park Commons, Script Capital, Foothill Ventures, Atlassian Ventures and Acequia Capital, but per-round attribution isn't public, so investors are left blank. Dates in rounds are first-sale dates from the filings.

companies.name: Orb
companies.description: Orb delivers a modern billing infrastructure that seamlessly powers revenue workflows for cutting-edge AI and software companies, simplifying financial processes so they can focus on innovation.
companies.website_source: company website (domain verified against name and accelerator description)
companies.funding_notes: Orb (withorb.com), San Francisco usage-based billing platform founded 2021 by ex-Asana engineers Alvaro Morales and Kshitij Grover. Raised a $5.1M seed led by Greylock (date not disclosed; announced together with the Series A) and a $14M Series A led by Menlo Ventures (announced March 2023), then a $25M Series B led by Mayfield in Sept 2024, which the company said brought total funding to $44.1M. Adyen agreed in June 2026 to acquire Orb for $335M in cash (deal expected to close July 1, 2026). Note: Payments Dive's line that Orb raised '$25 million' refers only to the Series B; the press releases put the total at $44.1M.

companies.name: Forethought
companies.website_source: company website (domain verified against name and accelerator description)
companies.funding_notes: Forethought (forethought.ai), San Francisco AI customer-support company and 2018 TechCrunch Disrupt Battlefield winner, co-founded by Deon Nicholas and Sami Ghoche. Rounds: $9M Series A led by NEA (Dec 2018), $17M Series B led again by NEA (Oct 2020), $65M Series C led by STEADFAST Capital Ventures (Dec 2021), and a $25M Series D strategic round led by Blue Cloud Ventures (May 2025), which the company said brought total funding to $115M. Note the four disclosed rounds sum to $116M; the total reported here is the company's own $115M figure. Zendesk agreed to acquire Forethought in March 2026 (terms not disclosed; expected to close by end of March 2026).

companies.name: Column Tax
companies.description: Tax filing, embedded in your app
companies.funding_notes: Column Tax (columntax.com), New York embedded tax-filing software/APIs for banks and fintech apps, founded 2021 by Gavin Nachbar (ex-Waymo) and Michael Bock. Raised a $5.1M seed led by Bain Capital Ventures with South Park Commons, Core Innovation Capital and Operator Partners (Nov 2021), then a $21.7M Series A led by Bain Capital Ventures (May 2022, per Forbes). The total here is the sum of the two sourced rounds; no later priced round was found. Other Series A participants were not verified from a primary source. Acquired by Aiwyn in Dec 2025 (terms not disclosed; Cooley advised Column Tax).

companies.name: Mayhem
companies.funding_notes: Mayhem (mayhem.gg), a San Francisco platform for running gaming-community leagues and tournaments (formerly Visor, an esports coaching tool), in Y Combinator's Winter 2018 batch; CEO and co-founder Ivan Zhou. TechCrunch reports that Accel led its 2018 Series A, with Afore Capital and NextGen Venture Partners also backing it. Axios reports $5.7M raised in total. The Series A amount (about $4.7M, Aug 2018) and an earlier ~$1M seed appear only in trackers, so the round amount is left null. Niantic acquired Mayhem on Jan 5, 2021 (terms not disclosed) and wound down the standalone product.

companies.name: Breez Security
companies.description: Identity threat detection in real time
companies.funding_notes: Breez (Breez Security), a New York identity threat detection, investigation and response (ITDR) startup founded in 2023 by Abhinav Srivastava (ex-CISO of Frame.io). The domain was not independently verified; the SPC page links a website, but it wasn't captured. BankInfoSecurity/ISMG (Oct 2025), citing the tracker IT-Harvest, says Breez 'received seed funding in January 2023 from Guiding Star Venture Capital and South Park Commons'. No amount or priced-round details are public, and SPC's involvement may be its Founder Fellowship check, so the round type is unclear. JumpCloud acquired Breez on Oct 23, 2025 (terms not disclosed). JumpCloud's CTO described it as a talent acquisition of a roughly four-person team.

companies.name: Gamma Networks
companies.description: Security training that adapts to behavior
companies.funding_notes: Gamma Networks, Inc. (Gamma.AI, gamma.ai), a San Francisco AI-powered security-awareness and cloud data-loss-prevention startup founded in 2018 (founder/CEO reportedly Arpit Goel). Palo Alto Networks completed its acquisition on Aug 11, 2021 for total consideration of $20.4M, primarily cash, per its SEC 10-Q. Gamma's technology went into Palo Alto's Next-Gen CASB and DLP. Trackers list a roughly $2.35M seed round (Nov 2018), but no press release, news report or filing confirming it was found, so no rounds are recorded.

companies.name: Reverie Labs
companies.funding_notes: Reverie Labs (reverielabs.com), a Cambridge, MA (Boston-area) company founded in 2017 by Jonah Kallenbach (CEO) and Ankit Gupta (CTO) that used machine learning to design brain-penetrant kinase inhibitors for cancer; a Y Combinator alum. Closed a $25M Series A led by Ridgeback Capital Investments with First Round Capital, Y Combinator and Neo in Feb 2021, which the company said brought total capital raised to more than $32M. The amount_raised is that 'more than $32M' floor. Pre-Series A rounds (about $7M) aren't itemized publicly. In Feb 2024 Ginkgo Bioworks acquired Reverie's key assets (AI infrastructure, software and models), and four team members including CTO Ankit Gupta joined Ginkgo; terms not disclosed.

companies.name: Galileo AI
companies.funding_notes: Galileo AI (usegalileo.ai), a San Francisco prompt-to-UI generative design tool founded by Arnaud Benard (ex-Google/Faire AI researcher) and Helen Zhou (ex-Facebook/Cruise designer). Announced a $4.4M seed led by Khosla Ventures in Feb 2024 with its public beta; angel backers included Julie Zhuo and Howie Liu. Alphabet told EU regulators under the DMA that it had acquired Galileo AI (MLex, March 2025; terms and closing date not public). The product was succeeded by Google Labs' Stitch, launched May 20, 2025, with co-founder Arnaud Benard among the Google authors. The domain comes from the product's public URL.

companies.name: Momentum
companies.funding_notes: Momentum (momentum.io), a San Francisco company founded in 2020 by Santiago Suarez Ordoñez, Ashley Wilson and Moiz Virani that turns sales calls, emails and Slack into structured revenue data. Raised a $5M seed led by Basis Set Ventures (closed Aug 2021, announced Nov 10, 2021) and a $13M Series A led by FirstMark Capital with Stage 2 Capital (July 2024), which brought total funding to $18M. Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Momentum on Feb 18, 2026 and completed the deal on March 2, 2026 (terms not disclosed).

companies.name: Jams
companies.funding_notes: Jams (jamshq.com; the company was Potrero Labs), a San Francisco generative-AI conversational-video app founded in 2022 by ex-Meta engineers Asad Awan and Hamza Aftab. Indus Valley Capital's portfolio page says it partnered with Jams at the Seed stage, and Nukta (Nov 2025, citing Reuters) says the company raised capital from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Indus Valley Capital. The seed amount, date and lead are not publicly reported; claims that a16z led the 2022 seed come only from social posts and are unverified. OpenAI acquired Jams in Nov 2025 (terms not disclosed). Only part of the team joined OpenAI, and the Jams and Hubble apps were set to shut down.

companies.name: Spindl
companies.funding_notes: Spindl (spindl.xyz), a web3/onchain ads and attribution platform founded in 2022 by Antonio García Martínez (early Facebook ads team); CoinDesk calls it Miami-based, while SPC lists it under San Francisco. CoinDesk (Oct 2022) reports it raised $7M co-led by Dragonfly and Chapter One with Polygon Ventures, Tribe Capital, Multicoin and angels. The 'seed' label comes from TokenInsight's headline. Coinbase announced on Jan 31, 2025 that it had acquired Spindl, which now runs under Base (terms not disclosed).

companies.name: Dashworks
companies.funding_notes: Dashworks (dashworks.ai), a San Francisco AI workplace search assistant founded in 2020 by Prasad Kawthekar and Pratyaksh (Praty) Sharma; Y Combinator W20. Raised a $4M round led by Point72 Ventures (Jan 2022, TechCrunch), then a $5M seed extension from Point72 Ventures (July 2023, VentureBeat as republished by Top Tech News), bringing total capital raised to $9M. No Series A was found. HubSpot agreed to acquire Dashworks on April 16, 2025 (terms not disclosed), and the team joined HubSpot's AI product group (Breeze).

companies.name: Satsuma
companies.funding_notes: Satsuma (satsuma.xyz), a San Francisco blockchain data-indexing/subgraph platform founded in March 2022 by Jonathan Kau (CEO) and Dan Li. Raised a $5M seed co-led by Initialized Capital and Archetype (April 2023). Alchemy acquired Satsuma in Sept 2023 (terms not disclosed); it became Alchemy Subgraphs and all six full-time employees joined Alchemy (The Block). Note: the SPC URL slug misspells the acquirer as 'alchemly'.

companies.name: Steady Health
companies.funding_notes: Steady Health (steady.health), a San Francisco virtual diabetes clinic built on continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), founded in 2018 by Henrik Berggren (ex-Dropbox); it launched in California in Jan 2020. Carbon Health announced the acquisition on June 4, 2021 (terms not disclosed; BusinessWire, Fierce Healthcare). Trackers report a roughly $3M seed (Sept 2018) with investors such as Wave Capital and Atlantic Labs, but no press release or reputable news report confirming it was found, so no rounds are recorded.
